To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we demonstrate for the first time a noninvasive, subsurface temperature measurement technique for turbid media with chemical selectivity and high accuracy, which can be used in a wide range of applications.

(1) we have developed a new analytical method, T-SORS, for the noninvasively measurement of temperatures within turbid media; (2) T-SORS has been conceptually proven by the first measurement of material-specific temperatures within turbid sublayers of PTFE; (3) the method has been demonstrated to achieve RMSEs of 0.1-0.8 °C over temperature ranges of 24-45 °C.
we have demonstrated a new analytical technique for the measurement of temperature within diffusely-scattering (turbid), translucent materials, with high chemical selectivty.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel analytical method for the measurement of subsurface temperature within diffusely-scattering media in combination with the capability of chemical selectivity.

the development of a new technique for noninvasive, subsurface, chemi Temperature Spatially Offset Stokes/anti-Stoke Raman Spectroscopic Imaging (T-SORSI) for the Measurement of Subsurface Temperature in Turbid Materials Using Anti-Stokes Light Scattering.
the development of a new analytical method, temperature spatially offset raman spectroscopy (T-Sors), for measuring subsurface temperatures within turbid media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method is a new analytical tool for the noninvasively, chemically specific measurement of temperatures in turbid media.
the proposed method is the first demonstration of a subsurface chemically specific temperature measurement within a turbid medium.
the proposed method, termed temperature spatially offset RSM, T-SORS, is a novel, noninvasive, and chemically specific technique for measuring subsurface temperatures within highly scattering media.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to measure the temperature of a subsurface layer in a turbid material by using the spatially offset anti-Stokes Raman scattering technique.
we have developed the first non-invasive technique for subsurface temperature measurements within diffusely (turbidly) scattering media in combination with a high level of chemical selectivity.
we have demonstrated a new technique that can measure the temperature of a turbid material (such as skin) from the outside.
The main takeaway from our work is that
temperature measurements can be made within turbid media using a combination of Stokes/ anti-Stokes light scattering and SORS.
the combination of Stokes/antis-Stokes light scattering and spatially offset RSM is a powerful analytical tool for measuring subsurface temperatures with a high degree of chemical specificity.
the combination of Stokes/antistokes light scattering with the recently developed SORS is a powerful tool for the noninvasively measurement of subsurface material-specific temperatures.
